projectSummary: Within-participant acute surface-EMG comparison of dumbbell bench, incline and shoulder presses in 12 trained and 12 novice collegiate-aged women, with the pectoralis major resolved into sternal and clavicular portions and each repetition phase analysed separately.

publication.statusSource: NCBI PubMed and PMC records fetched 2026-09-13; no retraction or correction notice

notes: Female-only sample, which is a genuine applicability strength for a claim set otherwise dominated by male participants, and a limit on generalising to men.
The clavicular result is phase-specific: it holds in the eccentric phase. A phase-specific difference is not a whole-repetition difference and is recorded as phase-specific.
Surface EMG is an acute activation measure and is not evidence of hypertrophy.

study.intervention: dumbbell bench press; dumbbell incline press; dumbbell shoulder press
study.population: Surface EMG was recorded from the dominant arm of 12 collegiate-aged resistance-trained women and 12 novice resistance-trained women during dumbbell bench, incline and shoulder presses, with average EMG amplitude computed for the concentric and eccentric phases of each repetition.

title: Shoulder Muscle Activation of Novice and Resistance Trained Women during Variations of Dumbbell Press Exercises
